problems.title: Percentage changes and component labels disagree with Tables 1 and \(3\)
problems.source_location: Results paragraph in §4.1, p. 7; Table 1, p. 8; Results paragraph in §4.2 and Table 3, p. 9.
claim: The results prose assigns numerical recall gains and ablation declines to the displayed metrics and components.
analysis: Table 1 gives Toys Recall@\(10\) as \(0.0781\); \(0.0462\) is NDCG@5. Relative Recall@\(10\) gain over TIGER is \(0.0781/0.0712-1\simeq9.69\%\). Industrial Recall@\(500\) gain is \(0.3716/0.2709-1\simeq37.17\%\), and Recall@\(800\) gain over the no-fusion variant is \(0.4466/0.2855-1\simeq56.43\%\). The text interchanges several component labels and improvement/drop denominators.

problems.title: The nearest-neighbor query must be the predicted dense vector
problems.source_location: §3.4, p. 6, Eq. (6), immediately after the dense query is defined in Eq. (5).
claim: Equation (\(6\)) supplies the discrete identifier to ANN after Eq. (\(5\)) defines the continuous query vector.
analysis:
The first argument of ANN is the generated discrete ID, although the surrounding procedure predicts a dense vector precisely to perform similarity retrieval. An ID can select an index partition, but it is not the continuous query vector whose cosine similarity to candidate embeddings is required. Figure 3 and Algorithm 1's similarity operation support a vector-query interpretation . A consistent replacement is \[
A_k = \operatorname{ANN}\bigl(\widehat v_k,
\{v_j:j\in C(c_k)\},N\bigr),
\] where \(c_k\) is the generated sparse ID and \(C(c_k)\) is the corresponding item bucket. If ANN also needs an index selector, write that as a separate argument with a declared signature. The returned object should contain item identities and their scores, rather than losing the item-embedding mapping. This is a confirmed error in the written equation, not evidence that the unavailable production code makes the same mistake.
result: The stated limitation or local discrepancy is supported within this source version. Stronger causal, historical-run or population conclusions remain unverified.
repair: Pass the predicted dense vector as the ANN query and the generated ID as a separate bucket selector.
problems.impact_rationale: This establishes the stated local correction or limitation. A consequential failure of the paper's central result has not been demonstrated.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: BeamFusion needs explicit normalization domains
claim: Equation (\(7\)) multiplies two normalized scores but does not state the index sets of the softmax operations.
analysis: Eq. (\(7\)) does not identify the two softmax normalization domains. One is presumably over generated IDs; the other could range over a full bucket, its retrieved subset or a pooled candidate set. These choices change cross-bucket rankings.

Let bucket masses be \(0.6,0.4\), similarities \(A:(0.90,0.89)\), \(B:(0.90,-1.00)\), and multiplier one. With separate retrieved-list normalization at \(N=1\), leading scores are \(0.6,0.4\), so \(A\) wins. At \(N=2\), they are approximately \(0.3015,0.3480\), so \(B\) wins without any changed model output. Truncated normalization is not inherently invalid, but must be specified and interpreted accordingly.
result: The stated limitation or local discrepancy is supported within this source version. Stronger causal, historical-run or population conclusions remain unverified.
repair: One complete factorization uses \(q_k=e^{\tau\ell_k}/\sum_re^{\tau\ell_r}\), \[r_k(j)=e^{\psi\cos(\widehat v_k,v_j)}/\sum_{u\in C(c_k)}e^{\psi\cos(\widehat v_k,v_u)}\], and \(s(j)=q_kr_k(j)\). This requires the full conditional partition function or a justified retained-mass correction.
problems.impact_rationale: This establishes the stated local correction or limitation. A consequential failure of the paper's central result has not been demonstrated.

problems.title: The disclosed fusion ablation changes support as part of the system
problems.source_location: §4.1 ablation paragraph, p. 8, with Tables 2 and 3, pp. 8-9.
claim: The no-BeamFusion condition replaces multiple sparse IDs with the single top ID before nearest-neighbor retrieval.
analysis: The no-BeamFusion variant uses one sparse ID; the full method uses several, changing both candidate support and scoring. If \(C_{\rm top1}(S)\) is the selected bucket, every restricted ranker satisfies \(\operatorname{Recall@K}\le\Pr\{Y\in C_{\rm top1}(S)\}\). For example, a first bucket covering \(60\%\) of true targets and a second covering the remainder permit a coverage gain without any benefit from the fusion formula.

The industrial no-dense variant additionally changes the semantic ID from two levels of \(32\) entries to three of \(256\). This is a legitimate alternative-system comparison, but it does not isolate removal of the dense branch.
result: The ablation measures the combined effect of its declared support/scoring change. It does not isolate the fusion formula alone, but this disclosed alternative-system comparison is not itself a current error.
problems.impact_rationale: No current-error impact: changing candidate support is part of the explicitly described ablation; its interpretation must remain at that combined scope.
problems.existing_correction_status: No paper repair is required for the disclosed combined ablation; formula-only causal attribution would need a different control.

problems.title: The entropy theorem needs a shared law and does not prove better fitted learning
problems.source_location: §3.5, Theorem 1 and the paragraph following it, p. 7; Appendix F, pp. 24-25.
claim: Theorem 1 and Appendix F compare independent and cascaded representations and interpret smaller entropy as a learning advantage.
analysis: For one fixed joint law \(P\) with the required finite entropies, \(H_P(ID\mid S)+h_P(V\mid S)-H_P(ID,V\mid S)=I_P(ID;V\mid S)\ge0\). This validates the same-law identity in Appendix F; independently fitted neural distributions need not share the marginals used in that comparison.

Lower fitted entropy does not imply better prediction. Fix a sequence \(S\). Let truth give probability \(1/2\) to \(ID=0\) with \(V\) uniform on \([0,1]\), and probability \(1/2\) to \(ID=1\) with \(V\) uniform on \([2,3]\). A cascaded fit with the same conditional unit-width uniform densities but ID probabilities \(0.999,0.001\) has joint mixed entropy about \(0.0079\) nats and expected negative log-density about \(3.4544\). An independent fit with uniform ID and equal mixture density on both intervals has entropy and expected negative log-density \(\log4\simeq1.3863\). Thus the lower-entropy fit is worse under the true law. This continuous-density construction respects the appendix’s differential-entropy setting and does not estimate COBRA’s performance.
result: The stated limitation or local discrepancy is supported within this source version. Stronger causal, historical-run or population conclusions remain unverified.
repair: Keep the valid shared-law conditional-information identity and remove unsupported fitted-learning implications.
problems.impact_rationale: This establishes the stated local correction or limitation. A consequential failure of the paper's central result has not been demonstrated.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: Baseline provenance and the nearest hybrid comparison remain unresolved
problems.source_location: §2, p. 3; baseline list and results, pp. 7-8; Appendix B, p. 22.
claim: The comparison section reports public baselines and discusses hybrid methods including LIGER.
analysis: All \(108\) baseline cells in COBRA Table 1 match the earlier TIGER paper's Table 1 exactly after aligning dataset order: nine methods, three datasets, four metrics. This comparison was performed against the official TIGER proceedings PDF, p. 7, not a third-party leaderboard . Reusing published baselines is legitimate; exact matching is not evidence of fabrication, plagiarism, or whether an author also reran a model. The necessary reporting correction is to distinguish copied published values from new reruns and identify the common evaluation protocol. Without that information, readers cannot evaluate feature parity, tuning budgets, or a paired significance comparison. LIGER is already cited in the paper as a hybrid generative/dense approach, but it is absent from both the public performance table and the industrial comparison. Its original paper and author repository confirm direct relevance . The currently available comparison does not establish superiority over the nearest hybrid alternative. This is an empirical gap, not proof that COBRA lacks novelty.
result: The available material identifies a scope or evidence gap; it does not prove that the reported empirical effect is false.
repair: Label inherited baseline sources and narrow claims to matched comparisons actually established.
problems.impact_rationale: The available evidence does not settle this concern, so it does not contribute to the paper's impact label.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: Missing configuration details prevent a unique reproduction
problems.source_location: §4.1 implementation details, p. 7; §4.2 implementation details, p. 9; Appendices C and E-G, pp. 23-25; checklist items 4-6, pp. 15-16.
claim: Implementation sections and the reproducibility checklist describe a repeatable method without releasing company code.
analysis: The paper identifies the public leave-one-out split and the industrial \(60\)-day/next-day split, along with some layer and codebook counts. Those are useful. However, the available manuscript does not give enough information to reproduce the reported training and inference: a named T5 checkpoint/tokenizer, embedding and hidden dimensions, attention-head counts, feed-forward dimensions, maximum history/text lengths, optimizer, learning-rate schedule, batch size, number of steps/epochs, checkpoint-selection rule, random seeds, and the actual M/N/temperature settings for each principal table are absent. There is also no full account of quantizer training and collision/invalid-code handling for the sparse-only variants. Evaluation details are similarly consequential. Appendix C.1 specifies the last item as the test target, but does not state whether ranking uses the full catalogue or sampled negatives, how training-seen items are filtered, or how ties are handled. In the industrial test, the unit over which recall is averaged and the definition of a relevant advertisement are insufficiently specified. The exact dates and availability rules for advertisements matter to a prospective deployment interpretation, although their absence is not proof of future-data leakage. This finding concerns missing information, rather than assuming that absent implementation details were handled incorrectly.
result: The available material identifies a scope or evidence gap; it does not prove that the reported empirical effect is false.
repair: Publish the missing model, training, selection, ANN and evaluation configuration without inventing unavailable company code.
problems.impact_rationale: The available evidence does not settle this concern, so it does not contribute to the paper's impact label.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: A traffic percentage does not determine significance
problems.source_location: online-results paragraph, p. 10; checklist item 7, p. 17.
claim: The online-results paragraph uses a \(10\)-percent traffic allocation to support statistical-significance language.
analysis: A \(10\%\) traffic allocation does not determine sampling variance. For \(p_C=0.01,p_T=0.01036\), equal arms of size \(N\) have uplift \(3.6\%\) and standard error \[\sqrt{[p_C(1-p_C)+p_T(1-p_T)]/N}\]. The standardized difference is approximately \(0.802\) at \(N=10^5\) and \(8.019\) at \(N=10^7\). These illustrative laws establish the need for arm sizes and variability; they do not reconstruct the industrial significance, which the checklist leaves unreported.
result: The available material identifies a scope or evidence gap; it does not prove that the reported empirical effect is false.
repair: Report arm sizes, randomization units, uncertainty and control/treatment definitions; a traffic fraction alone is insufficient.
problems.impact_rationale: The available evidence does not settle this concern, so it does not contribute to the paper's impact label.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: The diversity curve lacks a defined statistic and operating-point rule
problems.source_location: §4.3, p. 10, Figure 5 b and its discussion.
claim: Section 4.3 interprets Figure 5 b as a diversity/relevance balance controlled by fusion parameters.
analysis: The plot labels one axis as diversity without defining its calculation. The paper does not identify whether this is category count, entropy, catalogue coverage, inter-item dissimilarity, or a different quantity, nor the averaging unit and category level. These quantities can disagree substantially. Therefore the plotted relative improvements and the asserted best balance cannot be reproduced or interpreted quantitatively. The text also describes holding \(\phi\) fixed and tuning \(\tau\) and \(\phi\), whereas Eq. (\(7\)) makes \(\phi\) the model's beam score and uses \(\psi\) as the similarity coefficient. The likely correction is \(\psi\), but the authors should confirm the intended quantity and give its value.
result: The stated limitation or local discrepancy is supported within this source version. Stronger causal, historical-run or population conclusions remain unverified.
repair: Define the diversity statistic, averaging unit and validation operating-point rule.
problems.impact_rationale: This establishes the stated local correction or limitation. A consequential failure of the paper's central result has not been demonstrated.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: Transformer orders do not account for the full retrieval cost
claim: Appendix G Tables 5--6 give encoder/sequence-model complexity in support of scalable retrieval.
analysis: For \(H\) sparse tokens per item and history length \(L\), interleaving yields approximately \((H+1)L\) tokens. Standard dense prefill costs \(O(((H+1)L)^2D+(H+1)LD^2)\), reducing to the paper's \(O(L^2D+LD^2)\) when \(H\) is fixed. The displayed order is therefore not false for suppressing that fixed factor. A complete retrieval cost also includes beam/ID decoding, dense queries, index search, bucket scoring and selection. Exact bucket scoring costs \(O(D\sum_k|C(c_k)|)\); global scoring has a different catalogue term, and ANN cost depends on its index and recall target.
result: The available material identifies a scope or evidence gap; it does not prove that the reported empirical effect is false.
repair: Account separately for prefill, decoding, retrieval, indexing, selection and refresh cost.
problems.impact_rationale: The available evidence does not settle this concern, so it does not contribute to the paper's impact label.
problems.existing_correction_status: Proposed correction; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: Embedding plots do not identify the cause of recommendation gains
problems.source_location: Figures 4-6, pp. 9-10 and p. 24; Appendix D, p. 23.
claim: Figures 4--6 and Appendix D use cosine/t-SNE structure to interpret learned representations.
analysis: The cosine-similarity plots and t-SNE visualization are consistent with category organization. They do not by themselves establish that the organization causes the recommendation improvement. The difference matrix is described as quantitative confirmation, but the subtraction direction, ordering rule, number of sampled items per group, group labels, and aggregate cohesion/separation statistics are not stated.
result: The plots can legitimately illustrate representation structure. They do not identify a causal mechanism for the gains, but that inferential boundary is a clarification rather than a demonstrated false numerical result.
problems.impact_rationale: No current-error impact is assigned to this limitation of qualitative representation evidence.
problems.existing_correction_status: No paper repair is required merely because an illustrative embedding visualization does not establish causation.

impact_rationale: The supported findings concern local equations, released implementation details, reporting or bounded interpretation. No demonstrated failure of the paper's central result meets the stricter Major threshold.
